positions.name: Bitcoin (spot)
positions.catalyst: TWO FRESH, VERIFIABLE CATALYSTS FIRED OVERNIGHT AND THEY BOTH POINT THE SAME WAY. (1) THE US TREASURY EXPANDED LONG-END BOND BUYBACKS from roughly $2B to at least $4B per operation, starting September 2026. That is a structural, scheduled, forward-dated liquidity injection at the exact point on the curve that has been breaking markets — the 30-year printed 5.323% on Tuesday, a 19-YEAR HIGH. It pressured long yields and flipped risk appetite. (2) A WHITE HOUSE MEETING WITH CRYPTO EXECUTIVES plus regulators signalling clarity landed in the same 24 hours. THE TAPE CONFIRMED IT VIOLENTLY: Bitcoin jumped nearly 8% Wednesday, forcing more than $1 BILLION in short liquidations in about an hour, and roughly $2.99B of crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours of which ~$2.74B were SHORTS. Total crypto market cap +7.8% in 24h to $2.45 TRILLION. Ether +18% to $2,250, XRP +10% through $1.10. CRITICALLY, THIS IS NOT A ONE-PRINT SQUEEZE THAT FADED — BTC kept going overnight, from the ~$68.4K level implied by yesterday's 4pm equity close through the $69.5K headline print and on to $71,754 at run time, its highest since early June. Follow-through after the liquidation cascade is what separates a trend inflection from a squeeze that round-trips. THE STRUCTURAL LEG IS THE DEBASEMENT TRADE: US debt approaching $40 TRILLION, the largest monthly deficit since March 2021, and multi-decade-high long yields across the US, Japan, Germany and France. A Treasury that has to start buying its own long bonds back is the cleanest possible advertisement for hard-cap assets, and it is why this bid has a reason to persist past the short covering.
positions.driver: LONG SPOT BTC-USD AT 1x, 100% of capital, entry 71,754.10. THE INSTRUMENT CHOICE IS THE WHOLE DECISION TODAY AND IT WAS MADE BY THE CHASE RULE, NOT BY TIMIDITY. I wanted leverage on this catalyst. I could not get it at a price the mandate permits. Every levered crypto vehicle had ALREADY GAPPED PAST THE 8-10% NO-CHASE BAN before I could touch it: BITX (2x BTC) 15.01 vs a 13.66 close = +9.9%, AT the ban line. ETHU (2x ETH) 22.83 vs 19.48 = +17.2%, far past it. MSTR 114.30 vs 104.25 = +9.6%, past it, and carrying NAV-premium risk on top. COIN 172.44 vs 160.20 = +7.6% today on top of +11% yesterday, a ~19% two-day move in a single stock — technically inside the ban, excluded on downside protection. ETH spot itself is +18% and SOL at 87.12 is in the same extended cohort. THE UNDERLYING IS THE ONLY THING STILL CHEAP RELATIVE TO ITS OWN CATALYST: IBIT 40.64 bid vs a 38.78 close = +4.80%, which pins spot BTC at +4.8% versus yesterday's 4pm equity close — comfortably inside the ban while the 2x wrapper on the SAME asset is at +9.9%. Buying the 2x there is paying double for a move I can buy single. Taking the underlying is the disciplined answer, not the timid one: full participation in the catalyst, zero daily-reset volatility decay, zero equity-hours gap risk on a 24/7 asset whose catalyst is itself a 24/7 story, and the deepest liquidity of anything on the board. WHY I ROTATED OUT OF CRUDE AFTER TWO DAYS: UCO was profitable (+$60.92 today, +$266 the day before) but the thesis degraded on the specific point I flagged in yesterday's risks. Brent is toward $93, up more than 4% on the week and now SIX sessions into the run, against EIA's $85 Q3 forecast — the war premium I was being paid to hold is largely paid. And the de-escalation risk started to materialise VERBALLY: Trump said oil CONTINUES TO FLOW through the Strait and that he would be open to resuming talks with Tehran 'at some point.' That is the exact headline I said would cost 8% at 2x. Eight vessel attacks this month keeps it bid, but I am no longer being paid enough for a binary that is now leaning the wrong way. Re-entering a day-six run at +3.3% pre-market on softening rhetoric is the worst downside protection available today. CHOSEN OVER: (1) UCO again, reasoning above. (2) BITX 2x Bitcoin — same thesis, banned entry, and 2x daily reset into a post-liquidation tape is where the decay lives. (3) ETHU 2x Ether at +17.2% — the biggest mover on the board and the single worst risk/reward on it; ETH +18% in a day is a parabola, and 2x into a parabola is what I rejected NUGT for yesterday. (4) COIN and MSTR — high-beta crypto proxies with the same catalyst, both up ~19-24% over two sessions, both carrying single-name risk the underlying does not. (5) TMF 3x long Treasuries — the PUREST play on the actual root catalyst, since buybacks are literally a bid for long bonds. Rejected because the tape refused it: TMF is 31.15 bid vs a 31.59 close (-1.4%) and TMV 3x-short is UP ~1.1%, so long yields are RISING this morning despite the buyback news — crude at $93 is out-shouting it. 3x against a tape that just voted the other way is not a trade. (6) SOXL/SOXS — SOXL +0.9%, SOXS -1.1%, the Korean semi rout I passed on yesterday has fully stalled; no signal. (7) NUGT 2x gold miners at 185.15 vs 186.39, DOWN 0.7% — yesterday's parabola is already cooling, vindicating the pass. (8) SPXL 290.21 and FAS 176.99, both flat-to-down; TQQQ/SQQQ dead flat. The index is not the story. (9) WMT, BABA, DE, ROST earnings today — going 100% into a single-name print that lands in ~20 minutes is a coin flip, explicitly what this mandate warns against. (10) Jackson Hole with Warsh's first speech as Chair is Aug 27-29, OUTSIDE this window, so it is not tradeable today. (11) 100% CASH — rejected; there is a real, fresh, confirmed catalyst here, and the correct response to 'the levered version is too expensive' is to buy the unlevered version, not to sit out. EXECUTION NOTE — THE PRICE FEED FAILED FOR EQUITIES AGAIN AND I CAUGHT IT AGAIN: the dashboard proxy returned UCO 43.80, USO 130.91 and BITX 13.66, every one an EXACT match to the prior session's official close — the same pre-market stale-close pattern as the last two runs. Its CRYPTO leg, however, is genuinely live (crypto trades 24/7, so there is no stale close to serve): BTC-USD 71,754.10 stamped asOf 2026-08-20T10:43:23.810Z, seconds old at decision time, and moving between calls (71,788.93 then 71,754.10), which is the proof of life. That is the canonical entry. For the UCO exit I fell back to Robinhood real-time as the mandate directs: 45.21 = mid of a live 45.05/45.36 book at 2026-08-20T10:43:19Z, corroborated by an actual 45.25 pre-market print at 10:36:24Z and cross-checked against USO at 134.65/134.71 (+2.83%). Stop 64,578.69 (-10%, the spot-crypto band). Not a chase at +4.8%.
positions.risks: THE DOMINANT RISK IS THAT THIS IS A SHORT SQUEEZE WEARING A CATALYST'S CLOTHES. Roughly $2.74B of SHORTS were liquidated in 24 hours. Once that fuel is spent the mechanical bid vanishes, and squeeze-driven rallies characteristically give back half the move within a session or two. I am buying the day AFTER a $1B-in-an-hour liquidation cascade, which is structurally the same mistake I refused to make in NUGT yesterday — the only defences are that I am doing it at 1x instead of 2x, and that BTC kept climbing overnight rather than fading, which a pure squeeze usually does not. TECHNICAL LOCATION IS POOR: $71.75K is the highest since early June, so I am buying INTO overhead supply from every holder trapped at those levels, with a two-day move of roughly +11% behind me. There is real air beneath this. THE CATALYST HAS A TIMING GAP: the Treasury buyback expansion does not actually START until September 2026. Markets can and do front-run, then get bored — nothing mechanically supportive happens inside my 24-hour window, so between now and tomorrow's rotation this is pure sentiment and positioning. THE WHITE HOUSE MEETING IS A HEADLINE RISK IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: a readout that disappoints on regulatory clarity, or any hostile follow-up, unwinds the second catalyst instantly and crypto has no earnings or cash flow to catch it. THE BOND LEG IS ALREADY CONTRADICTING ME THIS MORNING: TMF is down 1.4% and TMV up ~1.1%, meaning long yields are RISING despite the buyback news. If the buyback story is being out-voted by $93 crude and the inflation impulse, then the primary macro pillar under this rally is weaker than the headlines suggest — and a renewed long-end selloff is precisely what has been crushing risk assets all month. CRUDE AT $93 IS ITSELF A THREAT TO WHAT I NOW OWN: the energy-led inflation impulse that made my last two days profitable is the same force that pushes real yields up and long-duration risk assets, including crypto, down. I have rotated from being long the cause to being long something the cause can hurt. OPPORTUNITY COST IS REAL AND I WANT IT ON THE RECORD: if I am right about direction, 1x captures roughly half of what BITX would have. The chase ban is what stopped me, and if BTC runs another 5% today that rule will have cost this book real money. I accept that — it is the same rule that has kept me out of two parabolas this week. 24/7 GAP RISK: spot crypto trades through the night with no circuit breakers and thin weekend-style liquidity in the small hours; a 10% adverse move can happen while nothing else is open, and my stop at 64,578.69 is a paper stop that cannot be worked. MITIGANTS: no leverage at all, on a day when leverage was the obvious temptation; an entry at +4.8% that is genuinely not a chase while the levered wrapper on the identical asset sits at +9.9%; the deepest liquidity available in the asset class; no daily-reset decay and no contango drag, unlike the crude ETF I just exited; a verified live crypto mark after catching the equity feed serving stale closes for the third run running; and a hard -10% stop.
